newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas up ahead of Taiwan tender.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas up ahead of Taiwan tender.

text.p: A gasoline buyer emerged to support the market just ahead of the close of Taiwan's import tender on Monday.

A Dutch trader bid the 95-octane unleaded grade at $23.50 per barrel fob lifting May 12-16, but offers still fell from Thursday's level. A Japanese trader offered the same timing at $23.75, lower than Thursday's $24.00 offer.
Buyers have been visibly absent from the fixed price market since the begining of the month and the appearance today was timely in light of Taiwan's tender closing, traders said.

In its last tender for HAN lifting from Madras on the east coast between April 25-27 which closed also on April 17, IOC only managed to secure only a $31 discount to Japanese spot quotes fob, from Dutch trader Vitol, compared to a $22.28 discount it received for a March 27-29 lifting cargo, industry sources said.
IOC's last HAN tender from Cochin, lifting April 1-3, was awarded at $19.08 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes, fob.
Naphtha prices were also steady to soft despite crude's gains amid ample supplies in the region.
Sri Lanka issued a tender to sell 110,000-125,000 barrels of light naphtha for May 2-3 lifting fob Colombo.
The tender closes on April 23 and bids are valid for two days.
In its last tender, CPC sold to Japanese trader Tomen 110,000-125,000 barrels of light naphtha at 88 cents per barrel below Singapore spot quotes, for March 24-25 lifting fob Colombo.
